generation_blueprint: Infer the electrical properties of three unknown strips using two observations from a single-loop circuit with two gaps. Use reliable contact and a good-conductor/insulator assumption to make the inference unambiguous.

student_question.stem:
Aisha makes a circuit with one battery, one bulb and two gaps, X and Y, in the same loop. She has three strips, P, Q and R. Each strip is either a good electrical conductor or an electrical insulator.

In each test, she places one strip across X and another across Y. Each strip touches both wire ends securely. The battery, bulb and wires work properly in both tests. Apart from the strips shown below, the circuit is unchanged.
student_question.diagram_alt: A single loop with one battery and one bulb. Two gaps, X and Y, lie in series in the same loop. A strip bridges each gap. There are no branches or bypass wires.
student_question.question: Which strips are electrical conductors?

answer.explanation_en: The bulb lights in Test 2, so both Q and R allow electric current to pass through them. In Test 1, Q is already known to be a conductor. With working components and secure contacts, the bulb not lighting shows that P breaks the conducting path under the stated conductor-or-insulator assumption. Therefore, Q and R are conductors and P is an insulator.
answer.scoring: Award 2 marks for option 3; otherwise 0. Confirm this proposed scoring with SIMCC before use.

distractor_rationales.issue: Treats R as an insulator even though Test 2 lights; also treats P and Q as conductors despite Test 1.
Treats Q as an insulator despite Test 2 lighting.
Ignores Test 1; all three conducting would make the bulb light in both tests.
